title: sfrecciare
definition: To move or pass very quickly.
example_it: Una moto è sfrecciata davanti a noi.
note: In the passato prossimo, it normally takes essere (e.g. è sfrecciata).

title: A seconda di / A seconda che
example_di_en: We'll decide depending on the circumstances.
example_che_it: Le pupille del gatto si dilatano o si restringono a seconda che ci sia poca o molta luce.
example_che_en: A cat's pupils dilate or constrict depending on whether there is little or a lot of light.
note: Use 'a seconda di' before a noun or pronoun. 'A seconda che' is rarer, is followed by the subjunctive, and is used when what happens next depends on which of two or more possible situations occurs.

title: azzardare
definition: To dare, venture, or risk saying or doing something despite uncertainty.
example_it: Non ti azzardare a mettere l'ananas sulla pizza! 🍕
example_en: Don't you dare put pineapple on pizza! 🍍🚫
note: Besides its transitive use (azzardare un'ipotesi), it is very common in the reflexive form 'azzardarsi', especially in expressions like 'Non ti azzardare a...!' meaning 'Don't you dare...!'.

title: Per quanto
definition: Means 'however much', 'no matter how', or 'although', depending on the context.
example_di_it: Per quanto ci provi, non riesce a convincerlo.
example_di_en: No matter how hard she tries, she can't convince him.
example_che_it: Per quanto fosse stanco, ha continuato a lavorare.
example_che_en: However tired he was, he kept working.
note: Can introduce either a concession ('although') or indicate degree ('however much'). Pay attention to the context and the verb mood.

title: accorgersi
definition: To notice, realize, or become aware of something.
example_it: Scusami, non me ne ero accorto.
example_di_it: Mi sto accorgendo di aver sbagliato.
example_di_en: I'm realizing I've made a mistake.
example_che_it: Mi sono accorto che Franco l'aveva già fatto ieri.
example_che_en: I realized that Franco had already done it yesterday.
note: Always used reflexively and takes essere in compound tenses. It commonly takes 'di' + noun or infinitive when referring to the same subject, or 'che' + a conjugated clause.

title: Tanto vale
definition: Means 'you might as well' or 'it's just as well', suggesting that one option is the most sensible or worthwhile given the circumstances.
example_che_it: A me la crosta della pizza non piace, tanto vale che sia ripiena.
example_che_en: I don't like pizza crust, so it might as well be stuffed.
note: 'Tanto vale' is commonly followed by the infinitive, but it can also be followed by 'che' + the subjunctive.
